references.text: God identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the same basis for obedience as in Leviticus 11:45
The same command to be holy: 'You shall be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy'
Repeats the call to holiness because the Lord is holy and has set Israel apart from the nations
God reminds that he made Israel holy and brought them out of Egypt to be their God
The promise that the Lord will take Israel as his people and be their God, linked to deliverance from Egypt
Israel shall be a holy people for the Lord, set apart from other nations
Israel is a holy people for the Lord, chosen to be his treasured possession
Israel is a holy people for the Lord their God, context for the purity laws
The seraphs cry 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts', confirming God's absolute holiness
Peter quotes this command directly: 'Be holy, for I am holy' as the basis for Christian conduct
Christians are called a holy people, a people whom God has acquired to proclaim his mighty works
Exhortation to pursue holiness, for without holiness no one will see the Lord
